# Open Science

## Open Science in the world

**The Open Science by UNESCO**

> Open science aims at making scientific knowledge openly available, accessible and reusable. The key elements of open science include: open access to scientific knowledge (including open access to scientific publications, data, educational resources, software and hardware); open infrastructures; open engagement with society and dialogue with indigenous and traditional knowledge systems, among others[^UNESCO].

[^UNESCO]: [UNESCO](https://www.unesco.org/en/open-science)

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column .center width=30%}
![](images/image-unesco-logo.png){width=80%}
:::

::: {.column width=70%}

UNESCO asks member States to :

**1.** Promote a shared understanding of open science and set out diverse paths to achieving it<br>
**2.** Develop an enabling policy environment for open science<br>
**3.** Invest in infrastructure and activities that contribute to open science<br>
**4.** Invest in training, education, digital literacy and capacity-building to support open science<br>
**5.** Foster a culture of open science and align incentives to support it<br>
**6.** Promote innovative approaches for open science at all stages of the scientific process<br>
**7.** Encourage international and multi-stakeholder cooperation in the context of open science to reduce gaps in technology and knowledge<br>
:::

::::

<!-- page -->

## Open Science in Europe

**The Open Science by EOSC**

> The ambition of the European Open Science Cloud, known as EOSC, is to develop a ‘Web of FAIR Data and Services’ for science in Europe. The implementation of EOSC is based on a long-term process of alignment and coordination pursued by the Commission since 2015.[^EOSC].

[^EOSC]: [EOSC](https://eosc.eu/)

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column .center width=30%}
![](images/image-eosc-logo.png){width=80%}
:::

::: {.column width=70%}

EOSC will also improve the situation for researchers in many ways, namely by :

**1.** Enhancing scientific research by providing access to a weath of data and research outputs from various fields and institutions.<br>
**2.** Fostering innovation by making it easier for researchers to share, collaborate and build on each others’ work.<br>
**3.** Improving transparency and reproducibility of research by making data and methods more open and accessible<br>
**4.** Reducing data silos and duplication of efforts by promoting data sharing and reuse<br>
**5.** Facilitating interdisciplinarity research and cross-sectoral collaboration by making data and resources from different domains more easily available<br>
:::

::::

<!-- page -->

## Open Science in France

**Second French Plan for Open Science**

> France is committed to ensuring that the results of scientific research are open to all, researchers, companies and citizens, without hindrance, without delay, without payment.[^french-plan]

[^french-plan]: [Second French Plan for Open Science](https://www.ouvrirlascience.fr/deuxieme-plan-national-pour-la-science-ouverte-pnso/)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column .center width=40%}
![](images/logo-PNSO2.png){width=60%}
:::
::: {.column width=60%}
**1.** Generalize open access to publications<br>
**2.** Structure, share and open research data<br>
**3.** Open and promote source codes produced by research<br>
**4.** Transforming practices to make open science the default principle<br>
:::
::::

<!-- page -->

## Open Science in France

**The French Open Science Strategy (OSS) 2026–2033**

> The French Open Science Strategy (OSS) 2026–2033, aims to strengthen the transformations initiated with the two previous national plans. Covering eight years, it is structured around ambitions, challenges, strategic objectives, and four-year action plans. The 2026–2029 action plan breaks down 8 strategic objectives into 30 actions and 75 measures.[^OSS]

[^OSS]: [The French Open Science Strategy](https://www.ouvrirlascience.fr/french-open-science-strategy/)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column .center width=20%}
![](images/image-OpenScienceStrategy.png){width=80%}
:::
::: {.column width=80%}
OSS Strategic objectives :

**1.**  Encourage a shift in practices to make open science the default approach<br>
**2.** Consolidate the governance and instruments of open science policy<br>
**3.** Reinforce the ecosystem of open science services and infrastructures, pillars of academic sovereignty<br>
**4.** Consolidate france’s position within the european and international open science landscape<br>
**5.** Structure and support open, reliable and high-quality academic publishing<br>
**6.** Consolidate the structuring of open and shared research data in accordance with the FAIR principles<br>
**7.** Increase the openness and valorisation of source code and software from research projects<br>
**8.** Ensure the transparency of clinical trials<br>
:::
::::

## Open science


:::: {.columns}

**Missions**

- To ensure the coordinated implementation, with higher education and research institutions, of the national open science strategy
- To enable the development of open science skills within the scientific community
- To coordinate France's actions in the field of open science at the European and international level
- Define the principles and guidelines for the use of funds from the National Open Science Fund
- Define the principles and guidelines for negotiations with the main publishers of scientific publications 
- To propose to the ministers responsible for research and higher education and to public authorities all actions likely to strengthen or promote access to knowledge, data, software and source code for research

## Legal context in France

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=80%}
<br />
The Law for a Digital Republic (**_LOI n° 2016-1321 pour une République Numérique (1)_**) is a French law promulgated on October 7, 2016. &nbsp;[{{< fa globe >}}](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000033202746)
:::

::: {.column width=10%}
:::

::: {.column width=10%}
![](images/journaux-officiels.jpg)
:::

::::


#### Article 30

> **This article grants authors the right to disseminate their research in open access.**


#### Article 533-4

::: {.small}
- **I.** Lorsqu’un écrit scientifique issu d’une activité de recherche financée au moins pour moitié par des dotations de l’État, des collectivités territoriales ou des établissements publics, par des subventions d’agences de financement nationales ou par des fonds de l’Union européenne est publié dans un périodique paraissant au moins une fois par an, **SON AUTEUR DISPOSE, MÊME APRÈS AVOIR ACCORDÉ DES DROITS EXCLUSIFS À UN ÉDITEUR, DU DROIT DE METTRE À DISPOSITION GRATUITEMENT DANS UN FORMAT OUVERT**, par voie numérique, sous réserve de l’accord des éventuels coauteurs, la **VERSION FINALE DE SON MANUSCRIT ACCEPTÉE POUR PUBLICATION**, dès lors que l’éditeur met lui-même celle ci gratuitement à disposition par voie numérique ou, à défaut, à l’expiration d’un délai courant à compter de la date de la première publication. Ce délai est au **MAXIMUM DE SIX MOIS** pour une publication dans le domaine des sciences, de la technique et de la médecine et de douze mois dans celui des sciences humaines et sociales.
- La version mise à disposition en application du premier alinéa ne peut faire l’objet d’une exploitation dans le cadre d’une activité d’édition à caractère commercial.
- **II.** Dès lors que les **DONNÉES ISSUES D’UNE ACTIVITÉ DE RECHERCHE FINANCÉE AU MOINS POUR MOITIÉ PAR DES DOTATIONS DE L’ÉTAT**, des collectivités territoriales, des établissements publics, des subventions d’agences de financement nationales ou par des fonds de l’Union européenne ne sont pas protégées par un droit spécifique ou une réglementation particulière et qu’elles ont été rendues publiques par le chercheur, l’établissement ou l’organisme de recherche, leur **RÉUTILISATION EST LIBRE**.
- **III.** L’éditeur d’un écrit scientifique mentionné au I ne peut limiter la réutilisation des données de la recherche rendues publiques dans le cadre de sa publication.
- **IV.** Les dispositions du présent article sont d’ordre public et toute clause contraire à celles-ci est réputée non écrite. 
:::



## Legal context in France

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=80%}
<br />
The Law for a Digital Republic (**_LOI n° 2016-1321 pour une République Numérique (1)_**) is a French law promulgated on October 7, 2016. &nbsp;[{{< fa globe >}}](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000033202746)
:::

::: {.column width=10%}
:::

::: {.column width=10%}
![](images/journaux-officiels.jpg)
:::

::::



:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=45%}
![[Guide d’application de la Loi](https://www.ouvrirlascience.fr/guide-dapplication-de-la-loi-pour-une-republique-numerique-pour-les-donnees-de-la-recherche/)](images/guide-loi.png){width=60% fig-align='center'}
:::

::: {.column width=10%}
:::

::: {.column width=45%}
<br />

This Law addresses the following elements:

- Accessibility
- Open Data and Data Portability
- Free software and Open formats
- Copyright issues
- Digital access for all
- Sovereign operating system (OS)
- Privacy
- etc.

:::

## Licenses

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=50%}
![](images/cc.png){width=60% fig-align='center'}
:::

::: {.column width=50%}
![](images/etalab.png){width=40% fig-align='left'}
![](images/licence-ouverte.gif){width=40% fig-align='right'}

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=50%}
**CC-BY 4.0**: This license enables reusers to distribute, remix, adapt, and build upon the material in any medium or format, so long as attribution is given to the creator. The license allows for commercial use. CC BY includes the following elements: BY: credit must be given to the creator.
<br/>
:::

::: {.small}
**Resources:** <https://creativecommons.org/share-your-work/cclicenses/>
:::

::: {.column width=50%}
**Etalab 2.0**[^1]: A license that fits within an international context by being compatible with the standards of Open Data licenses developed abroad and in particular those of the British government (Open Government Licence) as well as other international standards (ODC-BY, CC-BY 4.0).
<br/>
:::

::: {.small}
**Resources:** <https://www.etalab.gouv.fr/licence-ouverte-open-licence/>
:::
::::


[^1]: As part of the Government's policy to promote open data, Etalab has designed the "Open License". This license, developed in consultation with all stakeholders, facilitates and encourages the reuse of publicly available data.
